name: Salsa
notes: Salsa style pack (Doc 04 §3.2). Solo-first by design: timing + shines + styling carry a solo learner to social-ready; partnerwork nodes are flagged partner:true and their connection prep is trained solo. Pedagogy per Doc 02: start On1 (consensus), meet On2 later (Eddie Torres lineage — he built the first mambo syllabus in 1972 and named 500+ steps; named shines carry provenance in that spirit). Musicality core is ear training against clave and conga, not counting alone. The scene bridge is the studio social — the beginner-safe on-ramp the retention research identified.

seasons.finale: Film yourself clapping clave and stepping the basic through one full song — never off the 1.
Film a 4-shine sequence: basic, Suzy Q, Coca-Cola, flare kick — transitions on the 1.
Film 8 clean right turns in a row, spotted, landing on the 1.
Film your frame + cross-body footwork solo, then take ONE beginner class or lesson with a real partner.
Go to a salsa social. Dance three songs. That's the whole finale.

attributes.name: Clave ear L1
attributes.test: clap 2-3 clave through a full salsa song without losing it

attributes.name: Conga ear L2
attributes.test: find the conga slap on 2 and count 8s through a song you've never heard

attributes.name: Spotting L1
attributes.test: 10 consecutive spot turns, eyes snapping to one point, no stumble

attributes.name: Frame posture L1
attributes.test: 60s tall frame hold: ribs stacked, shoulders down, arms toned not stiff

nodes.name: Clave: the key (2-3 and 3-2)
checkpoints: clap the five clave hits over a track until it feels inevitable
hear which side is the 2 and which is the 3

nodes.name: Conga tumbao — the slap lives on 2
checkpoints: find the open tones on 4-and-8
the slap on 2 is your future On2 anchor

nodes.name: Song shape: montuno, mambo section, breaks
Cuban son → NY mambo → salsa; the Palladium and the barrio
Eddie Torres and the named-step tradition; On1 vs On2
Social etiquette: asking, thanking, floorcraft, the three-song rule of thumb
On1 basic (forward-back mambo step)
nodes.anchor: steps in days; ON the music in 2-4 weeks
checkpoints: break forward on 1 with the LEFT, replace on 2, together on 3 — pause on 4
back on 5 with the RIGHT, replace 6, together 7 — pause on 8
steps are small and under you — a salsa basic fits on a floor tile
weight fully changes on every step; the pause is a held weight, not a freeze
mistakes: stepping on 4 and 8 (the pause IS the style)

nodes.name: Side basic (lateral)
checkpoints: same 123-567 timing, traveling side to side
hips arrive AFTER the foot (Cuban motion seed)

nodes.name: Back basic & cumbia step
checkpoints: both breaks go behind — the polite crowded-floor basic
chest stays forward while feet rock back

nodes.name: Cuban motion (hip action from the floor)
checkpoints: bend-straighten the knees — the hips are a RESULT, never pushed
weight rolls through the whole foot, ball first
shoulders stay quiet and level while the hips speak
drill it standing still: weight changes only, no steps
mistakes: wagging the hips directly (reads instantly as fake)

nodes.name: Arm styling & body flow
checkpoints: arms move from the back, not the wrists
one arm frames while the other travels

nodes.name: Suzy Q
nodes.origin: swing-era step (the Big Apple, 1930s Harlem) adopted into mambo shines — one of the oldest names on the floor
checkpoints: cross-swivel: heel and toe trade as the feet cross and uncross
knees stay soft and together-ish; the twist is in the lower half
arms swing opposite in easy opposition
travels sideways a tile at a time, on timing

nodes.name: Coca-Cola
nodes.origin: classic NY mambo shine from the Palladium-era vocabulary
checkpoints: cross behind and unwind — the body spirals down and up
land the unwind ready on the 1

nodes.name: Flare kick & hook
nodes.origin: mambo shine staple; low flick, not a chorus-line kick
checkpoints: the kick is a flick from the knee on the break
hook lands you back into the basic without a hiccup

nodes.name: Stomps & syncopation (and-counts)
checkpoints: play the and-counts the basic normally skips
come home to the 1 like nothing happened

nodes.name: Pachanga taps (intro)
nodes.origin: from the pachanga craze (early 1960s NY, Charanga bands) — the bouncy heel-tap flavor
checkpoints: heel taps ride a down-bounce
it should look effortless and slightly mischievous

nodes.name: Shine sequence: 4 shines, one song
checkpoints: every transition lands on the 1 of an 8
basic between shines — home base is always there

nodes.name: Spot turn & spotting drill
checkpoints: pick a spot; head leaves last, arrives first
turn on the ball of ONE foot, other foot closes
finish facing your spot, on time

nodes.name: Right turn in the basic (1-2-3)
checkpoints: prep small on 7-8, turn over 1-2-3, together, resume
stay on your own tile — a turn travels nowhere
arms collect in, never fly out

nodes.name: Double turn
checkpoints: same tempo, twice the rotation — speed comes from the spot and the core, not the arms

nodes.name: Frame & connection (solo prep)
checkpoints: tone without grip: arms like springs, not clamps
connection comes from the back and center, hands just report it
drill on a doorframe/resistance band: give and receive pressure without collapsing

nodes.name: Cross-body lead (footwork both roles)
checkpoints: leader opens the lane on 2-3, follower travels 5-6-7
walk BOTH roles solo until the geometry is automatic
the lane is straight; nobody orbits

nodes.name: Led right turn (both roles)
checkpoints: the lead is a window, not a shove — hand offers, never pulls
follower owns her own balance through the turn

nodes.name: Copa (intro)
nodes.origin: NY On2 vocabulary staple from the Eddie Torres lineage

nodes.name: On2 conversion (break on 2, Eddie Torres timing)
checkpoints: same steps, new soul: break with the conga slap
dance one song On1, the next On2, until both feel like home

Dancing the song: hits, breaks, and letting the band lead
